title: Sri Lanka Name 15-Member Women's Squad for Pakistan ODI Series
excerpt: Captain Chamari Athapaththu leads a blend of experience and youth as Sri Lanka prepare for a crucial three-match home series against Pakistan in Hambantota, with ICC Women's Championship points at stake.
body:
• Sri Lanka have named a 15-member squad led by Chamari Athapaththu for the three-match ODI series against Pakistan starting July 23 in Hambantota.
  • Wicketkeeper Anushka Sanjeewani and opener Vishmi Gunaratne have been recalled, while teenage pacer Rashmika Sewwandi earns her maiden ODI call-up.
  • The series is part of the ICC Women's Championship 2025-29 cycle, with Sri Lanka currently third in the standings on eight points.
  • All three matches will be played at the Mahinda Rajapaksa International Cricket Stadium on July 23, 25, and 28.

Sri Lanka Cricket on Friday announced a 15-member squad for the upcoming three-match ODI series against Pakistan Women, with veteran all-rounder Chamari Athapaththu confirmed as captain. The home series, scheduled for July 23, 25, and 28 at the Mahinda Rajapaksa International Cricket Stadium in Hambantota, forms part of the ICC Women's Championship 2025-29 cycle and carries significant qualification implications for the next Women's ODI World Cup.

Key Recalls and a Fresh Face

The most notable selection decisions involve the return of experienced wicketkeeper Anushka Sanjeewani, who last represented Sri Lanka at the 2025 ODI World Cup before being dropped in favour of Kaushani Nuthyangana. Nuthyangana has now been omitted from the squad, with Sanjeewani reclaiming her place behind the stumps.

Opening batter Vishmi Gunaratne, who missed Sri Lanka's last ODI assignment — a 2-1 series victory against Bangladesh in April — due to injury, has also returned to the fold. Her presence at the top of the order alongside Hasini Perera gives the side a more settled look.

Teenage fast bowler Rashmika Sewwandi is the squad's sole new addition, earning a maiden ODI call-up. Her inclusion comes at the expense of Malki Madara, while Piumi Wathsala and Sugandika Kumari have also been left out.

Riding T20 World Cup Momentum

Sri Lanka enter the series on the back of a promising ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 campaign in England, where they finished third in Group B, narrowly missing the semi-finals after being edged by West Indies on net run rate. Athapaththu was the team's standout performer, amassing 164 runs in five matches at an average of 43.00, headlined by an unbeaten 106 off just 61 balls against Ireland — the first-ever century scored in a Women's T20 World Cup run chase.

"Most of the experienced players have been retained as Sri Lanka look to carry their good form into the 50-over format."

— Sri Lanka Cricket selectors' statement

The selectors have broadly retained the core group that impressed at the World Cup. Nilakshika Silva, who contributed vital innings through the tournament, keeps her place in the middle order. All-rounders Kaveesha Dilhari and Hansima Karunaratne provide batting depth and bowling variety, while left-arm spinner Inoka Ranaweera remains the spearhead of the bowling attack in ODI cricket. Young spinner Dewmi Vihanga, who showed promise during the T20 World Cup, has also been retained.

One notable absentee is 19-year-old fast bowler Mithali Ayodhya, whose distinctive sling bowling action and four-wicket haul made her one of the breakout stars of the T20 World Cup. She has not been included in the ODI squad for this series.

Championship Race Heats Up

The series carries added weight because of its role in the ICC Women's Championship 2025-29 standings. Sri Lanka currently sit third with eight points from six matches, level on points with both Pakistan and West Indies. New Zealand lead the table with 13 points from nine matches. A strong result against Pakistan at home would bolster Sri Lanka's prospects of qualifying directly for the next ODI World Cup.

For the South Asian cricket diaspora, the series provides a rare chance to watch two familiar rivals compete in the 50-over format under the championship framework. Both teams will be eager to collect points, and the head-to-head rivalry adds an extra layer of intrigue for fans across the subcontinent and beyond.

Full Squad and Schedule

Sri Lanka squad: Chamari Athapaththu (c), Vishmi Gunaratne, Hasini Perera, Harshitha Samarawickrama, Hansima Karunaratne, Kaveesha Dilhari, Nilakshika Silva, Anushka Sanjeewani, Chethana Vimukthi, Inoka Ranaweera, Nimasha Meepage, Imesha Dulani, Dewmi Vihanga, Rashmika Sewwandi, Kawya Kavindi.

Schedule:
1st ODI — July 23, Hambantota
2nd ODI — July 25, Hambantota
3rd ODI — July 28, Hambantota

Pakistan's squad for the tour is yet to be confirmed. Both teams will be aiming to build momentum ahead of a packed calendar of ICC Women's Championship fixtures over the coming months.
